current_text.html: The censure of deposition shall be administered by the moderator in the words following: Whereas, ____________________, a teaching elder of this Presbytery (or ruling elder or deacon of this church), has been proved, by sufficient evidence to be guilty of the sin of ____________________, we, the ____________________ Presbytery (or Church Session), do adjudge him disqualified for the office of the Christian ministry (or ruling eldership, or deaconship), and therefore we do hereby, in the name and by the authority of the Lord Jesus Christ, depose from the office of a teaching elder (or ruling elder or deacon) the said ____________________, and do prohibit him from exercising any of the functions thereof. If the censure includes suspension or excommunication, the moderator shall proceed to say: We do moreover, by the same authority, suspend the said ____________________ from the Sacraments of the Church, until he shall exhibit satisfactory evidence of sincere repentance, or We do moreover, by the same authority, exclude the said ____________________ from the Sacraments, and cut him off from the fellowship of the Church. The sentence of deposition ought to be inflicted with solemnities similar to those already prescribed in the case of excommunication.

relationships.title: Presbytery jurisdiction and restoration path for a deposed and repentant minister

occurrences.excerpt: The CCB advised that restoration of a deposed minister follows BCO 37-4 and 37-7 exclusively, and BCO 18–21 ordination procedures do not apply.

relationships.title: Ordination status and restoration process after deposition from office

occurrences.excerpt: The CCB advised that a deposed officer has no ordination status, and restoration requires at minimum reaffirmation of vows, laying on of hands, and a proper call.

metadata.synopsis: South Florida Presbytery deposed a Teaching Elder, suspended him from the sacraments, and later excommunicated him without first assigning him to a particular church under BCO 46-8. The complainant argued that omission stripped Presbytery of jurisdiction. The SJC denied the complaint: BCO 46-8 requires assignment but fixes no timeframe or mechanism; a deposed minister remains under Presbytery's jurisdiction until transfer, and BCO 37-9(a) preserves censure authority. Deferring under BCO 39-3, the SJC found no clear error in Presbytery's efforts. Two concurrences agreed in result but disputed the majority's broad reasoning and deference.

The SJC denied a complaint challenging Nashville Presbytery's decision not to indict a teaching elder for allegedly sinful teaching on homosexuality and same-sex attraction. The adopted judgment held that the 147-page record showed Presbytery fulfilled its BCO 31-2 investigatory duty and did not show it erred in judgment when it declined process; the complaint was denied 20-0-1. Concurring opinions raised concerns about committee recusal, record clarity, and exegetical uses of Scripture, but they were separate and did not alter the denial.

metadata.synopsis: North Florida Presbytery restored a minister deposed for adultery by a 19–17 vote. The SJC sustained the complaint, holding that Presbytery had not proceeded with the required caution and that a bare majority could not demonstrate BCO 34-8’s required strongly favorable general sentiment. It declined to require reordination, calling that question unsettled and treating BCO 37-5’s restoration pronouncement as sufficient pending clarification. The SJC annulled Presbytery’s actions concerning the minister and remanded for a proper probationary and review process.

Sherfey challenged James River Presbytery’s denial of his complaint and alleged errors in its commission’s proceedings. The SJC ruled the complaint judicially out of order with incurable defects: several grounds had not first been adjudicated by Presbytery as BCO 43-2 required, and the General Assembly filing missed BCO 43-3’s thirty-day deadline. Incorrect advice from Presbytery’s clerk did not excuse compliance. The adopted decision neither reached the merits nor ordered a remand; only a concurrence proposed returning the matter to Presbytery.

metadata.synopsis: Chastain appealed Heritage Presbytery’s 2006 excommunication and deposition. The SJC held the appeal judicially out of order because Chastain had renounced PCA jurisdiction on May 8, 2006. Consequently, Presbytery’s later proceedings were moot and SJC 2005-1 remained in effect. The SJC did not reach the merits. A concurrence questioned the discipline process after renunciation; a dissent argued the majority lacked constitutional authority to recognize unilateral withdrawal and thereby undercut discipline.

metadata.synopsis: TE John P. Clark, Jr. appealed his conviction for contumacy and suspension/deposition by Southwest Presbytery's Judicial Commission. The SJC found the appeal in order (17-4) and remanded the case for retrial (21-0) on grounds that the Judicial Commission committed significant procedural errors, including abandoning original charges and convicting Clark of contumacy on new charges without giving him opportunity to respond.

relationships.title: Clark v. Southwest Presbytery (Request for Clarification)

metadata.synopsis: John P. Clark, Jr. requested clarification of the SJC decision in Case 93-5 regarding who controls the assets of South Valley Presbyterian Church, Inc. after the congregation voted to withdraw from the PCA. The SJC held it lacked jurisdiction over the civil corporate entity and its property, declining to rule on Clark's request.

occurrences.excerpt: At the regularly stated meeting of MVP on February 20, 1990, MVP took action to excommunicate Mr. Stringer from the fellowship of the church according to BCO 36-7.

metadata.synopsis: Randy Stringer appealed his excommunication by Mississippi Valley Presbytery after being deposed and then excommunicated for failure to respond to the presbytery. The SJC set aside the excommunication and remanded the case to MVP, holding that after deposition the presbytery was required under BCO 46-8 to assign Stringer to membership in a particular church rather than proceed to excommunication. Dr. Morton H. Smith dissented, arguing that the presbytery had proper grounds to proceed to excommunication after Stringer's contumacy.
